safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about workplace behaviors, conditions, or practices that may impact health and safety. These observations are typically made by workers, supervisors, or safety personnel during routine checks or daily activities, and can include both positive and negative findings related to safety compliance or risks.
examples: Observed all workers wearing required PPE in the welding area.
Noted that emergency exits were clear and unobstructed during shift.
Identified a missing guard on the conveyor belt during routine inspection.
Observed forklift operator following proper speed limits in the warehouse.
Noticed a spill in the loading dock promptly cleaned up by staff.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are critical to report and analyze because they reveal underlying hazards or unsafe conditions that could lead to future incidents if not addressed.
examples: A falling tool narrowly missed a worker passing below.
Forklift reversed into a walkway but stopped before hitting anyone.
Chemical container slipped but was caught before spilling.
Worker tripped over a hose but regained balance without falling.
Overhead load swung out of control but did not strike any equipment.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker sustained a laceration while using a box cutter.
Forklift struck a storage rack causing minor property damage.
Employee slipped on wet floor and sprained ankle.
Chemical spill required evacuation of the lab area.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short in equipment.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or danger in the workplace. These reports are used to alert management and safety teams to risks that need to be assessed and controlled before they cause incidents.
examples: Reported exposed wiring near the main switchboard.
Identified unguarded machinery in the production area.
Noted oil spill on the workshop floor as a slip hazard.
Reported blocked fire extinguisher access.
Observed damaged handrail on the stairs.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition, event, or behavior that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or resource use. In HSE, these observations help monitor compliance with environmental standards and identify areas for improvement.
examples: Observed oil leaking from equipment onto the ground.
Noted improper disposal of chemical containers in waste bins.
Identified excessive dust emissions from the crusher area.
Reported noise levels exceeding permitted limits near the compressor.
Observed recycling bins overflowing in the break area.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any observation or report of a product, process, or service not meeting required standards or specifications. In HSE, quality issues can have safety or environmental implications if defective materials or processes lead to hazards.
examples: Found welds not meeting inspection criteria on pressure vessel.
Reported incorrect labeling on chemical drums.
Identified faulty safety harnesses in equipment storage.
Observed paint peeling from newly coated surfaces.
Noted missing documentation for batch release.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal or informal notification to repair, service, or inspect equipment, infrastructure, or safety systems. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures that could lead to safety incidents or environmental harm.
examples: Requested repair of leaking valve in the pump room.
Submitted work order for malfunctioning emergency lighting.
Reported broken guardrail on loading dock for maintenance.
Requested inspection of overhead crane after unusual noise.
Notified maintenance about faulty fire alarm panel.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that increases the risk of injury, illness, or damage. Reporting unsafe conditions is essential in HSE to enable corrective actions before incidents occur.
examples: Found wet floor with no warning signs in hallway.
Observed missing machine guards on press.
Noted poor lighting in stairwell.
Identified exposed nails on wooden pallets.
Reported blocked emergency exit door.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the likelihood of an accident or injury. In HSE, unsafe acts are observed and reported to address risky behaviors and reinforce safe work practices.
examples: Worker climbed ladder without using fall protection.
Employee bypassed machine safety interlock.
Observed operator not wearing required eye protection.
Worker used forklift to lift personnel without cage.
Employee smoked in a designated no-smoking area.
